question: Should OpenClaw add a public per-target subagent concurrency config, and if so should it live under `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` rather than top-level `agents.list[].maxConcurrent`?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds a new public config/default surface and scheduler semantics in an area where repository policy requires maintainer intent before adding config knobs.

options.title: Add scoped per-target cap
options.body: Implement `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` as the canonical per-target subagent cap while preserving the existing global subagent lane limit.

options.title: Fold into broader lane work
options.body: Keep this issue open but make the broader lane-isolation design own both per-target caps and named subagent lanes to avoid duplicate config surfaces.

options.title: Decline the config knob
options.body: Document the existing global cap and prompt-level workaround, accepting that users cannot serialize one local-model subagent independently.

recommendation.title: Add scoped per-target cap
recommendation.body: Implement `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` as the canonical per-target subagent cap while preserving the existing global subagent lane limit.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and recently reviewed the central concurrency resolver and already engaged with this issue's config/runtime gap.
